sources.title: Morph public model metadata
sources.evidence: Exact morph-v3-large entry names v3 Large Apply, describes complex code editing, and declares text input/output, 262144 input-context tokens and 131072 output tokens. Its created timestamp is shared across current entries, so is not treated as a launch date.

sources.title: Morph complete API documentation: Apply API and Code Apply API
sources.evidence: Apply tables explicitly distinguish morph-v3-large from morph-v3-fast and auto. Large is for complex changes; requests carry original code, edit snippet and optional instructions, and return merged code. Full-document exact-variant occurrences were inspected; no exact-variant parameter count, backbone classification or explicit negative reasoning/tool capability classification was found.

sources.title: Fast Apply: Code Merging at 10,500 tok/s for AI Agents
sources.evidence: March 5, 2026 page distinguishes Large at 5000+ tok/s from Fast at 10500+ tok/s, with both listed at 262K context. Describes external agent planning and code merging. Generic 7B statements accompany the 10500 tok/s offering and do not explicitly assign a count to the Large row.

sources.title: Morph Models
sources.evidence: Separates hosted open-weight general coding models from specialized agent models, explicitly listing morph-v3-large as Fast Apply (large) for difficult edits.

sources.title: Morph End User License Agreement
sources.evidence: January 13, 2026 EULA covers Morph services and model weights where applicable, grants limited revocable use, and characterizes underlying Morph models and weights as proprietary technology. Open-source components are exceptions only when separately identified.

sources.title: Optimizing Models to Be Fast at Codegen
sources.evidence: June 19, 2026 first-party research discusses Fast Apply, trained speculators and optimized serving. It gives no morph-v3-large total/active count or exact backbone. Counts for hosted open models and example drafters are not Large specifications.

sources.title: Fast Apply Makes Faster Agents
sources.evidence: November 4, 2025 article search-index text describes attention/feed-forward kernels, pruned vocabulary and hierarchical positional encodings for Fast Apply generically; no exact Large specification is established. Direct page currently exposes title/date/table of contents without article body, so indexed text is treated as limited evidence.

sources.title: Morph Gets Faster: 10,500+ Tokens Per Second
sources.evidence: Dated June 15, 2025. Both web extraction and browser inspection expose title/date and table of contents but not article body. This access limitation prevents checking whether its model-selection section establishes earlier Large availability; it does not verify July 7.

sources.title: Morph V3 Large API Pricing and Providers
sources.evidence: Catalog lists July 7, 2025 as Released and identifies the code-apply model. This corroborates the catalog date but is not an original developer launch announcement and does not establish earliest public availability.

sources.title: Models.dev Morph V3 Large catalog entry
sources.evidence: Baseline lead was inspected. Its comment says lab metadata was carried over from the OpenRouter catalog; it asserts July 7 and false reasoning/tools without cited primary capability classification, and contains the unsupported generic flagship description.

name.note: Normalized display name of the exact morph-v3-large / v3 Large Apply entry.

developer.note: Morph identifies the specialized apply model as its own; AutoInfra, Inc. is the legal entity.

family.note: Catalog family grouping for Morph V3 apply models; does not imply a disclosed base architecture.

release_date.note: 2025-07-07 is corroborated as a provider-catalog date, not verified as earliest developer release. The potentially relevant June 15 developer article lacks its body in direct extraction and browser. Clear the exact date rather than equating provider listing with original launch.

open_weights.note: Morph places this model in its specialized API lineup; its own models/weights are proprietary under the EULA, with separately identified open components excepted. No open-weight release is identified for this variant.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the Morph model service under the EULA; not an assertion that separately served third-party open models use this license.

parameters_b.note: The generic Fast Apply 7B claim cannot be assigned confidently to v3 Large: the same page ties it to 10500 tok/s and lists Large separately at 5000+. Exact model tables and later research do not resolve the mapping. No sibling count transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-parameter count is disclosed for v3 Large in the reviewed primary model tables, API documentation or later research. Neither dense structure nor total-equals-active is assumed.

architecture.note: Generic Fast Apply discussion mentions specialized merging architecture and serving kernels, but does not establish the exact Large backbone or dense/MoE classification. FP8 and speculative decoding are serving properties, not sufficient architecture evidence.

context_window.note: Exact first-party model metadata specifies max_context_length 262144 tokens. Some integration/provider limits differ; retain the explicit direct model metadata value.

modalities.note: Exact metadata explicitly declares text input and output; API merges source-code text.

reasoning.note: Fast Apply is classified as specialized merging with planning performed upstream, but no exact-variant explicit negative reasoning-mode classification was verified. Missing reasoning keys do not prove false; clear the baseline boolean.

tool_call.note: The model is invoked inside another agent edit tool and returns code, but that is not an explicit declaration that the model cannot issue structured tool calls. No exact primary negative classification was verified; clear false rather than infer it from absent metadata.

description.value: Specialized code-edit application model that merges edit snippets into existing source files, intended for complex changes.
description.note: Replaces the unsupported general-purpose flagship claim with the exact developer-described apply role; avoids mixed speed/accuracy claims.

patch.description: Specialized code-edit application model that merges edit snippets into existing source files, intended for complex changes.
patch.notes: V3 Large is a specialized code-apply model, distinct from V3 Fast and Morph-hosted general coding models. Generic Fast Apply 7B statements are not clearly assigned to Large; total parameters and backbone remain unverified, and active parameters are not disclosed in reviewed sources. July 7, 2025 is a provider-catalog date, not a verified original release. Reasoning/tool-call support remains unverified because absent metadata is not a negative classification. Current documented specifications were checked; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Corrects the description to specialized code editing and adds proprietary licensing. Confirms exact first-party 262144-token context and text modalities. Clears unsupported exact release date and negative reasoning/tool-call assertions. Total size and architecture remain unresolved because generic Fast Apply disclosures do not identify v3 Large; active count remains undisclosed in reviewed sources.
